title: From Reactive to Real-Time: Rethinking Finance Visibility in Modern Organizations
body_text: In this article, we unpack how real-time transaction data can transform financial management by shifting teams from reactive to proactive decision-making. We’ll also show how Boya’s live dashboard equips organizations with the tools to monitor, control, and forecast spend in real time. ‍ The Visibility Gap in Traditional Finance Processes ‍ ‍ According to a 2023 survey by Gartner, 60% of finance leaders cite delayed visibility into expenses as a top challenge impacting cash flow management . This challenge is amplified in organizations with decentralized teams, multiple payment channels (cards, mobile wallets, bank transfers), and fast-paced procurement needs. Traditionally, businesses rely on static reports: Spreadsheets updated days or weeks later Delayed expense claims and reconciliations Manual budget monitoring that fails to capture ongoing shifts The result? Leadership often learns about overspending after it’s too late to course-correct. Budget owners can’t confidently track spend against targets, and finance teams spend more time investigating issues than driving strategy. ‍ Why Real-Time Spend Visibility Matters ‍ ‍ The shift to real-time spend visibility delivers three key benefits: ✅ Better Forecasting : When you can see every transaction as it happens, cash flow forecasting becomes more accurate. You can adjust spending plans immediately based on real-time trends rather than outdated reports. ✅ Tighter Cost Control : With live transaction data, managers can spot overspending early, freeze budgets if needed, or adjust allocations on the fly. It also minimizes the risk of fraudulent or non-compliant spending going unnoticed. ✅ Improved Accountability : Department heads, team leads, and even individual employees get visibility into their spending patterns, making budget ownership a daily practice—not a month-end surprise. A report by The Hackett Group found that companies using real-time spend analytics reduce budget variances by up to 25% , driving more predictable financial performance. ‍ Inside Boya’s Real-Time Dashboard ‍ ‍ At Boya, we’ve designed our spend management platform around one core principle: live data leads to better decisions . The Boya dashboard gives finance teams and department leaders instant access to: Live transaction feeds across cards, M-Pesa, and bank transfers Policy alerts that flag non-compliant spending in real time Custom spend breakdowns by department, project, or cost center Forecasting widgets that visualize spend pace versus budget targets Instead of waiting until the 30th of the month, managers can log in daily—or set automated alerts—to monitor spend trends and react quickly. Whether it’s noticing rising travel costs mid-month or proactively tightening vendor payments, Boya shifts finance teams from firefighting to forecasting . ‍ The Strategic Payoff: Scale with Confidence ‍ ‍ In a previous blog, Scaling Your Business with Effective Expense Management , we explored how scaling businesses often outgrow traditional finance processes. Without timely visibility, the risks of uncontrolled spending, cash flow issues, and poor unit economics multiply rapidly. Real-time visibility is the antidote: Founders get peace of mind knowing cash runway is accurate CFOs can confidently report numbers to investors Managers can optimize spending decisions without waiting for finance It’s not just about seeing spend—it’s about steering the company’s financial health in real time. ‍ Conclusion: Moving from Reactive to Proactive Finance In 2025, operating with a 30-day financial delay is no longer acceptable. Real-time spend visibility isn’t a nice-to-have—it’s a competitive advantage. Companies that embrace live expense monitoring unlock sharper forecasts, tighter controls, and greater accountability across teams. Boya’s dashboard empowers organizations to move from reactive to proactive, giving every stakeholder—from finance teams to department heads—the tools to drive smarter, faster decisions. 💡 Ready to see how real-time spend visibility can transform your business? title: A Technical Breakdown of Jolt's Cryptography (and the exploit)
summary: The mathematics of the missing Dory commitments behind the Jolt exploit.
body_text: Breaking Down Jolt Cryptography The Mathematics Behind the Exploit Jul 13, 2026 #zkvm #cryptography This is a technical analysis of the Dory vulnerability that was found and poc’d by our agent. This blog goes much deeper into the mathematics behind how the exploit actually worked. If you’ve landed in the wrong blog, you can read how our AI found it here . TL;DR Ordering of Fiat-Shamir in Sumcheck Missing constraint in the Dory proving library Exploiting the constraint and backsolving from the Fiat-Shamir ordering is_seven(6) == true (6 == 7) About Us At Veria Labs, we build AI pentesting agents that automatically find and fix security vulnerabilities in your application. Founded by members of the #1 competitive hacking team in the U.S., we’ve found critical vulnerabilities in every company we’ve worked with, from small startups to enterprise giants. Think we can help secure your systems? We’d love to chat! Book a call here . What is Jolt? We’ve covered Jolt in our other blog but in brief, Jolt is a zkVM for RISC-V built as a general purpose zkVM for proving arbitrary executions. While it can be used as a standalone library, Jolt is expected to be the backbone of the new Zero L1 chain currently being developed by LayerZero. Jolt will facilitate private payments on the Zero network. This allows anyone to verify transactions without seeing details like wallet addresses, amounts, etc. Vulnerability Details This section covers the math, the vulnerabilities, and how they were chained. As always, this may get quite messy. Background From a program to polynomials : A zkVM proves “this program ran correctly and produced this output.” Jolt encodes the execution trace as a family of multilinear polynomials {Pi}i∈[m] over the BN254 scalar field 𝔽=𝔽r, where each Pi:𝔽n→𝔽 is the multilinear extension of its values on the boolean hypercube, Pi(𝐱)=∑𝐛∈{0,1}nPi(𝐛)∏k=1n(xkbk+(1−xk)(1−bk)),𝐱∈𝔽n. Checking the program reduces to checking a system of claims over the {Pi}. Sumcheck. The sumcheck step certifies that a polynomial g=∑iλigi sums to a claimed value C over the hypercube without the verifier recomputing the sum: C=?∑𝐱∈{0,1}ng(𝐱),λi=ℋ(τ)∈𝔽. It runs one variable at a time. In round j the prover sends the univariate restriction gj(X)=∑𝐱∈{0,1}n−jg(r1,…,rj−1,X,𝐱), the verifier enforces the fold gj(0)+gj(1)=cj−1 against the running claim, samples a challenge rj∈𝔽, and updates cj=gj(rj). After n rounds the protocol collapses to a vector of opening claims at the random point 𝐫=(r1,…,rn). {Pi(𝐫)=vi}i∈[m],vi∈𝔽, Sumcheck is interactive however. To turn this non-interactive, Jolt applies a Fiat-Shamir transcript across all steps to sample the randomness. Jolt derives every challenge by hashing the running transcript τ of prover messages: rj=ℋ(τ<j). Security relies on this binding invariant. Anything that can change whether the proof is accepted must be absorbed into τ before the challenge that depends on it: ∀accept-relevant w:w→τ before r=ℋ(τ). Polynomial commitments ( Dory ). The openings Pi(𝐫)=vi are discharged by a polynomial commitment scheme. Jolt batches its polynomials under powers of a challenge γ into one instance (𝒞∗,𝐫,y∗) with 𝒞∗=∑iγi𝒞i, and proves it with Dory. Dory is a pairing based scheme, also developed by a16z, over 𝔾1,𝔾2,𝔾T with a pairing e:𝔾1×𝔾2→𝔾T. Dory asserts that a committed polynomial 𝒞∈𝔾T satisfies P(𝐳)=y with a final pairing identity of the form ∏ke(Lk(𝐳),Rk)=𝒞⋅e(⋅,e2), where e2∈𝔾2 encodes the claimed value. The Ordering of Fiat-Shamir in Sumcheck The ZK sumcheck fixes its random challenges before the prover commits to the hidden output claims. The batching coefficients λ are drawn up front, the round polynomials are folded to produce 𝐫, and only afterwards are the hidden output claims added into the transcript: 1 let batching_coeffs = transcript . challenge_vector (sumcheck_instances . len ()); // λ ← H(τ) [early] 2 // … n sumcheck rounds fold r_1..r_n out of τ … 3 let oc_committed = pedersen_gens . commit_chunked ( & output_claim_values, rng); // Com(v_i; ρ_i) 4 transcript . append_commitments ( b"output_claims_coms" , & output_claims_commitments); // τ += Com(v) [late] By the time the openings 𝖢𝗈𝗆(vi;ρi) enter τ, every challenge that will test them is fixed. Write 𝝌=(λ,𝐫,…) for those challenges and Φ(𝐯,𝝌)=0 for the BlindFold output constraint the openings must satisfy. There’s no way around this ordering: the output claims are values p(𝐫), and 𝐫 (like λ) is the sumcheck’s challenge stream, so the claims don’t exist until the challenges that produce them are already drawn. Binding the openings is intended to be left entirely to the Stage 8 opening proof. Technically, that does give a modified prover some help. With 𝝌 known first, and Φ affine in each opening, changing one coordinate vk by δ moves the constraint along a straight line, Φ(𝐯+δ,𝐞k,,𝝌);=;Φ(𝐯,𝝌)+δ⋅∂vkΦ,∂vkΦ≠0, so the offset that lands it back on zero is just δ⋆=−,Φ(𝐯,𝝌)/∂vkΦ. The prover shifts the hidden opening and re-commits; the only thing that changes is the freshly-formed 𝖢𝗈𝗆(vk;ρk), which nothing has constrained yet: 1 let delta_i = (target_output_claim - base_eval) * derivative_i . inverse () . unwrap (); // δ* = -Φ/∂Φ 2 output_claim_values[output_index] += delta_i; // v_k ↦ v_k + δ* 3 * opening_value += delta_i; But by design this isn’t supposed to work: the Stage 8 Dory opening is supposed to reject any 𝐯 whose openings don’t match the real polynomials Pi at 𝐫. The Vulnerability: Missing Constraint in Dory Dependency Jolt calls the Dory library for all proving/verifying related to Dory. In Dory’s zk verifier, it never ties the proof to the point it is supposed to be evaluated at. Stage 8 first collapses all the committed polynomials into a joint opening (𝒞∗, 𝐫, y∗) with 𝒞∗=∑iγi𝒞i, and hands it to verify_zk with the point 𝐫 but no value, since in ZK the evaluation stays concealed as ycom=𝖢𝗈𝗆(y∗;⋅): 1 let hiding_evaluation_commitment = PCS :: verify_zk ( 2 & joint_commitment, pcs_opening_point . as_slice (), // (C*, r) ; no y* 3 & proof . joint_opening_proof, & preprocessing . pcs_setup, transcript) ? ; Following this call into the Dory function dory-pcs::verify_evaluation_proof in the dependency, the whole thing turns on a single group element e2∈𝔾2 that anchors the final pairing identity. In the transparent (non-ZK) path, e2 is built from the claimed value which ties both the value y and the point 𝐳 into the equation: (𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭)e2=y⋅g2,verify ∏ke(Lk(𝐳),Rk)=𝒞⋅e(⋅,e2). In ZK mode though, it reads e2 from the proof and discards y entirely: (𝐳𝐤)e2←π.e2 (prover-chosen),y unused,ycom←π.ycom. 1 #[cfg(feature = "zk" )] 2 let (e2, is_zk) = match ( & proof . e2, & proof . y_com) { 3 ( Some (pe2), Some (yc)) => { /* sub-proofs about y_com only */ ( * pe2, true ) } 4 ( None , None ) => (setup . g2_0 . scale ( & evaluation), false ), 5 _ => return Err ( DoryError :: InvalidProof ), 6 }; 7 #[cfg(not(feature = "zk" ))] 8 let (e2, _is_zk) = (setup . g2_0 . scale ( & evaluation), false ); // e2 binds `evaluation` The side proofs check that ycom is a well formed commitment, but they never check that it actually commits to P∗(𝐳). So with e2 as a free group element the prover supplies, the acceptance relation stops depending on 𝐳 altogether: ∃π:V(𝒞∗,𝐳,π)=1 for every 𝐳∈𝔽n. The Full Exploit For the PoC, our agent setup a simple Rust program of: 1 fn is_seven (x : u64 ) -> bool { 2 x == 7 3 } with the goal of forging a proof to claim is_seven(6) == true . Since the vulnerability allows an attacker to forge a Dory proof, the first observation on the ordering of the sumcheck can be backsolved before abusing the Dory commitment. The attack runs in 2 main steps. Let 𝐲∗∈{0,1}8 be the public output region. In an honest case: 𝗂𝗌_𝗌𝖾𝗏𝖾𝗇(6) produces y0∗=0 (false). First, flip the public output bit (from false to true) and rewrite the single store instruction that writes it, so the trace claims the flipped value: y0∗↦y0∗⊕︎1,rewrite the unique 𝖲𝖡/𝖲𝖧/𝖲𝖶/𝖲𝖣→𝚙𝚘𝚜𝚝_𝚟𝚊𝚕𝚞𝚎. The witness is now internally inconsistent since the BlindFold constraint breaks (Φ(𝐯,𝝌)≠0) An honest prover would abort on 𝐀𝐳∘𝐁𝐳≠𝐂𝐳. Because the sumcheck never bound the claim values, solve for the offset that puts the broken constraint back to zero and shift the hidden output opening by it: δ∗=−Φ(𝐯,𝝌)/∂vkΦ,vk↦vk+δ∗ ⇒ Φ=0,Ξ(⋅) fixed. The prover now holds a coherent but false claim set, with a forged joint value y^∗≠P∗(𝐫). The forged claim no longer matches the real polynomial at the honest point. But a multilinear polynomial is degree ≤1 in each coordinate, so its value moves linearly as you sweep one coordinate. This means you can solve for a single alternate coordinate rℓ′ at which the real polynomial hits the forged value exactly: 𝐫′=𝐫 with rℓ′=y^∗−P∗(𝐫|zℓ=0)P∗(𝐫|zℓ=1)−P∗(𝐫|zℓ=0) ⟹ P∗(𝐫′)=y^∗. The prover emits a perfectly honest Dory opening at this wrong point, π←𝗈𝗉𝖾𝗇_𝗓𝗄(P∗,𝐫′). The verifier checks at the honest point 𝐫. Since Dory’s ZK check ignores the point, it accepts anyway (V(𝒞∗,𝐫,π)=1). This was run against an unchanged verifier and both honest and forged proofs: 𝚑𝚘𝚗𝚎𝚜𝚝.𝚋𝚒𝚗→𝖮𝗄 (y0∗=0),𝚙𝚘𝚌.𝚋𝚒𝚗→𝖮𝗄 (y0∗=1):6=7. Impact in the zkVM This is a total break of soundness in ZK mode. For an arbitrary false statement S there exists an constructible π with 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒zk(S,π)=1, against the unchanged verifier. The transparent path, binding both y (via e2=y⋅g2) and 𝐳, is unaffected. Since Jolt is used as a general purpose zkVM as well as being the backbone of the Zero L1 chain, this makes it the highest impact for a zkVM. On the blockchain, depending on how it will be used, can most likely be used to forge false transactions or introduce an infinite mint. Remediation Patching the Dory vulnerability can be done in either the library or Jolt itself. Bind the opening point. The cleanest fix would be to directly patch this on the Dory library side. That said, there is a comment that claims the caller must bind this before calling any Dory functions. So, to fix this on the Jolt side, we can apply the patch: 1 --- a/crates/jolt-dory/src/scheme.rs 2 +++ b/crates/jolt-dory/src/scheme.rs 3 @@ fn open_zk(poly, point, _eval, setup, hint, transcript) { 4 let ark_point: Vec<ArkFr> = point.iter().rev().map(jolt_fr_to_ark).collect(); 5 + // Bind the opening point before Dory derives its challenges. 6 + transcript.append(&LabelWithCount(b"zk_dory_point_bind", point.len() as u64)); 7 + for p in point { 8 + p.append_to_transcript(transcript); 9 + } 10 let mut dory_transcript = JoltToDoryTranscript::new(transcript); 1 --- a/crates/jolt-dory/src/scheme.rs 2 +++ b/crates/jolt-dory/src/scheme.rs 3 @@ fn verify_zk(commitment, point, proof, setup, transcript) { 4 let ark_commitment = jolt_gt_to_ark(&commitment.0); 5 + // Mirror the prover: bind the same point before verification draws challenges. 6 + transcript.append(&LabelWithCount(b"zk_dory_point_bind", point.len() as u64)); 7 + for p in point { 8 + p.append_to_transcript(transcript); 9 + } 10 let mut dory_transcript = JoltToDoryTranscript::new(transcript); With this in place an honest proof still verifies, and a proof produced at a different point is rejected: verify at correct point = Ok(...) verify at wrong point = Err(VerificationFailed) Conclusion This is a result of feature and a missing check that were chained together to fulfill the full exploit chain. While each on there own are not exploitable, exploiting both at the same time allows for complete proof forgery. The Dory vulnerability was reported to a16z which was quickly patched. Fixes from the team are listed here: On the Jolt side, https://github.com/a16z/jolt/pull/1664 and on the Dory side: https://github.com/a16z/dory/pull/23 PoC All files related to the PoC can be found in this GitHub repo: https://github.com/verialabs/Jolt-PoC

title: The Science of Workout Variety: Why It Keeps You Consistent
summary: Does workout variety help you stay consistent? Science says yes. Here are 5 research-backed reasons variety beats boredom and makes the habit stick.
body_text: The Science of Workout Variety: 5 Reasons Doing Something Different Helps You Stay Consistent Variety is not a luxury. It is the mechanism that keeps a workout habit alive. Short answer: Yes, workout variety helps you stay consistent. Research links varied training to better exercise adherence, mostly because it fights the boredom that makes people quit. Mixing up how you train (different machines, formats, and intensities) keeps you mentally engaged and physically progressing, so the habit actually sticks. Here is the part nobody tells you: if you have quit a workout routine before, it was probably not a willpower problem. Most fitness equipment is engineered to be boring, while the phone in your pocket is engineered to be irresistible. You were never in a fair fight. The good news is that the same science that explains why you quit also points to a fix, and it is not "try harder." It is variety. In this article Does workout variety really help you stay consistent? Why most people quit (and why it is not willpower) 5 science-backed reasons variety keeps you consistent But isn't consistency more important than variety? How to get variety without buying five machines Frequently asked questions Does workout variety really help you stay consistent? It does, and the effect is bigger than most people expect. Boredom is one of the most reliable predictors of dropping out of a fitness program, and variety is the direct antidote. When researchers compare high-variety and low-variety programs, the high-variety groups tend to stick with it longer, and the effect is driven by how much variety people feel they are getting, not just what is on paper. The chain is simple: people repeat what they enjoy, variety increases enjoyment, enjoyment increases adherence, and adherence is what creates results. A recent 2024 study found that adding structured variety to a routine improved motivation, self-efficacy, and how positively people felt about exercise, and they reported feeling more autonomous and confident too. Novelty is also doing something in your brain. New challenges nudge the dopamine system that drives learning and reward , which is a big reason a fresh workout feels more engaging than the fiftieth identical session. Why most people quit (and why it is not willpower) Roughly half of new gym members quit within six months, and a large share of memberships go essentially unused. Home equipment tells the same story. The rower, the bike, or the treadmill arrives with big plans attached, and by month two it has quietly become an expensive clothes rack. That moment has a name: the motivation cliff. The cliff is not a character flaw. It is what happens when repetitive equipment collides with a brain that craves novelty. Do the same 20 minutes of steady cardio every day and your body adapts, the challenge fades, and your mind checks out. This is where variety stops being a "nice to have" and becomes the thing that keeps you showing up. It is also why Aviron built game psychology into the machine itself, and why 92% of Aviron members are still working out a year later , a number that looks almost impossible next to those industry dropout rates. A rower brings a completely different stimulus than a run or a ride: full-body, low-impact, and easy to make playful. The variety engine, in one machine Aviron Strong Rower Full-body, low-impact rowing with 1,000+ games, classes, and scenic routes so no two sessions feel the same. Free 30-day home trial · Financing available Shop the Strong Rower → 5 science-backed reasons variety keeps you consistent 1. It kills boredom, the number one reason people quit Boredom is not a minor annoyance. It is a leading driver of dropout. Variety keeps the experience novel, and novelty keeps your brain's reward system switched on. That is the difference between "I have to work out" and "I get to play the next level." 2. It breaks plateaus so you keep seeing results Your body follows the SAID principle: Specific Adaptation to Imposed Demands. Do the same thing and you adapt to exactly that thing, then progress stalls. Changing the movement, tempo, or intensity is a form of progressive overload. In fact, groups that varied their training have made greater gains in muscle size and strength than those who repeated an identical plan. Results keep coming, and visible results are rocket fuel for consistency. 3. It protects you from overuse injuries Repeating the same movement pattern loads the same joints and tissues over and over, which is how overuse injuries start. Cross-training spreads the load across different muscle groups and planes of motion. Fewer tweaks and flare-ups means fewer forced breaks, and nothing wrecks a streak like being sidelined. For more ideas, see our guide to the best low-impact exercises to add to your routine . 4. It turns exercise into something you actually enjoy Enjoyment is not fluff. It is the single best predictor of whether you will still be training months from now. Varied routines score higher on enjoyment, autonomy, and self-efficacy, the belief that you can actually do this. When a workout feels like a choice instead of a chore, you stop needing to hunt for motivation every single day. 5. It flexes to real life Some days you have 40 minutes and energy to burn. Some days you have 12 minutes and a toddler. Variety lets you match the workout to the day: a hard interval session when you are fired up, an easy scenic row or walk when you are wiped. A routine that bends to your life is a routine you keep, and this is exactly why so many people ask how to make workouts less boring in the first place. What to vary What it changes Easy example The machine Which muscles and joints do the work Row Monday, ride Wednesday, walk Friday The format Mental engagement and pacing Game one day, coached class the next, scenic route after that The intensity The training stimulus and recovery Hard intervals, then an easy steady session The duration How the workout fits your day 12 minutes when busy, 40 when you are not Same treadmill, dozens of formats: a coached class today, a game tomorrow, a scenic walk the day after. Walk, run, or race a game Aviron Victory Treadmill Incline walks, interval runs, coached classes, and games on one screen, so cardio never turns into a chore. Free 30-day home trial · Financing available Shop the Treadmill → But isn't consistency more important than variety? This is the right question, and the answer is that they are not rivals. Consistency is the goal. Variety is one of the best tools for reaching it. The mistake is thinking you must choose. You do not. It is also worth busting a myth here. "Muscle confusion," the idea that constantly shuffling exercises keeps your muscles guessing, is mostly marketing. Muscles do not get confused. Structured progression and steady practice are the real drivers of results. Randomly changing everything every single day can actually slow you down, because your body never gets to adapt to anything. The sweet spot is a stable framework with planned variety inside it. As a rough guide: Experience level Change the core plan every... But add small variety... Beginner 6 to 12 weeks Session to session (format, game, route) Intermediate 4 to 6 weeks Weekly (intensity and duration) Advanced 3 to 4 weeks Within each session (intervals, targets) In other words, keep the skeleton steady and let the day-to-day workouts stay fresh. That is variety in service of consistency, not against it. How to get variety without buying five machines Here is the practical problem: real variety usually means a gym full of equipment or a closet full of gadgets you will not use. That is expensive, and it reintroduces the friction that made you quit last time. The fix is to put the variety inside the machine instead of across a room full of them. That is the entire idea behind Aviron. Every machine runs the same Engagement Engine: 1,000+ workouts spanning science-backed games, coached classes, streaming, scenic virtual routes, and multiplayer competition, plus 300+ Les Mills workouts. One rower can be a boat race on Monday, a HIIT class on Wednesday, and a calm scenic paddle on Sunday. That is more genuine variety than most people ever get from a gym, without leaving your living room. It is also why fitness entertainment actually works where willpower alone does not. Then there is variety across the whole lineup. Rowing, cycling, and running each bring a different stimulus, so choosing your modality by the day is variety at the highest level. Add the Abs Hero for core-focused sessions and you can cover cardio, strength, and recovery from home. Ride a race, a class, or a route Aviron Fit Bike S Game-powered cycling with classes, scenic rides, and leaderboards to keep every session different. Free 30-day home trial · Financing available Shop the Fit Bike S → The proof it works: 50,000+ members, 4,000,000+ workouts completed, an average rating of 4.8 to 4.9 stars, and 92% of members still training a year later. That is what happens when variety is built in, not bolted on. Frequently asked questions How often should I change my workout routine? Change the core structure of your plan every 4 to 6 weeks for most people. Beginners can wait 6 to 12 weeks to build a foundation, and advanced exercisers may switch every 3 to 4 weeks. Keep smaller variety (formats, games, intensity) going in every session so it never gets stale. Is workout variety the same as muscle confusion? No. "Muscle confusion" is a marketing term, and muscles do not actually get confused. Real workout variety is about training different muscles and movement patterns, staying mentally engaged, and applying progressive overload. The benefits are real; the "confusion" branding is not. Can too much variety hurt your progress? Yes. If you change everything every day, your body never adapts to anything, and progress stalls. The sweet spot is a stable plan with planned variety inside it: same weekly framework, different workouts within it. Does workout variety help beginners or only advanced exercisers? It helps beginners most of all, because beginners are the ones most likely to quit. For a new exerciser, keeping the routine enjoyable and engaging matters more than optimizing every set. Variety is what gets you to the consistency where results are built. What is the easiest way to add variety at home? Change one variable at a time: the format, the intensity, or the length. A machine with built-in games, classes, and scenic routes does this for you automatically, which is the whole point of Aviron's game-powered workouts . If you want a deeper fix for boredom, see how to prevent workout boredom . Make boredom impossible Try any Aviron machine at home. If the variety does not keep you coming back, send it back.
